description: This group contains two images. The captioned Fig. 2 (second image) is a three-panel finite-element simulation set-up. (a) is a square EBSD-derived 2D representative volume element phase map - blue Austenite matrix with red δ-Ferrite regions and elongated yellow TiB2 particles - annotated with corner letters a, b, c, d, edge arrows labelled up, down, left and right, reference-point markers RP-2 (left edge) and RP-1 (right edge), and a small x-y coordinate axis. (b) is the 2D finite-element model drawn as a perspective stack of planar slices labelled γ-Fe, γ-Fe/TiB2 PB, TiB2, δ-Fe/TiB2 PB and δ-Fe, with the legend Austenite (blue), δ-Ferrite (red), TiB2 (yellow). (c) is a circular close-up of the local mesh: a regular quadrilateral element grid resolving a blocky yellow TiB2 particle in blue austenite with red δ-ferrite patches; a dashed arrow links it to (b). Together (a)-(c) show how a real EBSD phase map becomes a periodic, mesh-resolved 2D plane-strain RVE for the FEM calculation. The first supplied image is printed as panel "(c)" but is instead a materials-selection chart of SYS × UE (MPa g⁻¹ cm³) versus specific modulus (GPa g⁻¹ cm³) for literature lightweight steels, with red ("Our LDS"), orange ("Fe-TiB2 steel") and black ("IF steel") reference stars; it does not match the Fig. 2 caption.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a square phase map whose blue Austenite matrix contains red δ-Ferrite regions and elongated yellow TiB2 particles.

Panel (a) identifies the four model edges by node-set letters (a top-left, b top-right, c bottom-right, d bottom-left) together with arrows labelled up, down, left and right, and marks RP-2 on the left edge and RP-1 on the right edge.
Panel (a) carries a small x-y coordinate axis at its lower-left corner, indicating the map is a 2D section.
Panel (b) is drawn as a perspective stack of planar model slices with leader labels reading γ-Fe, γ-Fe/TiB2 PB, TiB2, δ-Fe/TiB2 PB and δ-Fe.
The colour legend shared by panels (b) and (c) reads Austenite (blue), δ-Ferrite (red) and TiB2 (yellow).

Panel (c) is a circular magnified inset showing a regular grid of square finite elements over a large blocky yellow TiB2 particle set in blue Austenite and intersected by red δ-Ferrite regions; a dashed arrow links it to panel (b).

The second supplied image is a scatter chart plotting SYS × UE (MPa g⁻¹ cm³) on the ordinate (gridlines 4 to 22, step 2) against Specific modulus (GPa g⁻¹ cm³) on the abscissa (gridlines 20 to 36, step 2), with shaded property envelopes and many open-symbol literature data points.

In that chart the red star labelled 'Our LDS' lies between the 32 and 34 specific-modulus gridlines at a SYS × UE value just below the 10 gridline; the black star 'IF steel' lies between the 26 and 28 gridlines near the 6 gridline; an orange star 'Fe-TiB2 steel' lies in the mid-30s region between the 7 and 8 gridlines.

A large legend panel lists the literature alloys by family (Fe-Mn-Ti-B, Fe-Ti-B-(Nb), Fe-Cr(-Ni)-B(-Cu/C), Fe-Mn-Al-C-(Si/Mo/V), Fe-(Zr/Hf/V/Nb/Ta/Mo/W)-B, Fe-Mn-Al-Ti-B) with individual compositions and heat-treatment conditions, and lists the three reference stars under 'Reference materials'.

The caption identifies the three FE panels as an EBSD-based representative volume element with its boundary conditions (a), the 2D finite element model (b) and a close-up of the local finite-element meshes (c).

The citing text states that the RVE is two-dimensional, built from EBSD image pixels by an automatic meshing/phase-assignment mapping algorithm, and that its dimensions match the 200 μm side length of the selected EBSD image.

The citing text states that the mesh type is CPE4 and that a mesh size of 0.4 μm was used, corresponding to 500 × 500 elements, exceeding the reported minimum of 250 × 250 elements for a 200 μm × 200 μm RVE.

The citing text states that periodic boundary conditions were applied to the boundary nodes, with nodal sets a (up), b (down), c (left) and d (right) and reference points RP-1 (load applied) and RP-2 (fixed).
The citing text states that a second RVE with identical TiB2 distributions and boundary conditions but consisting solely of α-ferrite was prepared to simulate conventional Fe-TiB2 steel.

subfigures.description: EBSD-based square 2D representative volume element phase map: blue Austenite matrix with red δ-Ferrite regions and elongated yellow TiB2 particles. Boundary-condition annotation: corner letters a (top-left), b (top-right), c (bottom-right), d (bottom-left); arrows labelled up, down, left and right outside the corresponding edges; markers RP-2 (left edge midpoint) and RP-1 (right edge midpoint); red x-y axes at the lower-left corner.

2D finite element model rendered as a perspective stack of planar model slices, with leader labels reading γ-Fe, γ-Fe/TiB2 PB, TiB2, δ-Fe/TiB2 PB and δ-Fe. Legend beneath: Austenite (blue), δ-Ferrite (red), TiB2 (yellow). A dashed line points to panel (c).

Circular magnified close-up of the local finite-element mesh: a regular grid of square elements (CPE4-type quadrilaterals) resolving a large blocky yellow TiB2 particle, surrounded by blue Austenite and cut by red δ-Ferrite patches. No scale bar or element-size annotation is printed.

Materials-selection scatter chart: ordinate SYS × UE (MPa g⁻¹ cm³) with gridlines 4-22 (step 2), abscissa Specific modulus (GPa g⁻¹ cm³) with gridlines 20-36 (step 2). Shaded envelopes and numerous open-symbol data points for literature alloys, two dashed guide curves, and three reference stars: red 'Our LDS', orange 'Fe-TiB2 steel', black 'IF steel'. A large legend panel lists alloy families Fe-Mn-Ti-B, Fe-Ti-B-(Nb), Fe-Cr(-Ni)-B(-Cu/C), Fe-Mn-Al-C-(Si/Mo/V), Fe-(Zr/Hf/V/Nb/Ta/Mo/W)-B and Fe-Mn-Al-Ti-B with individual compositions. This chart is unrelated to the Fig. 2 caption.

unreadable_items: Grouping ambiguity: the first supplied image is printed as panel '(c)' and shows a materials-selection chart unrelated to the Fig. 2 caption; its own figure number is not visible in the crop.
Panel (a): the small circle markers attached to the RP-1 and RP-2 labels are partially cropped at the image borders.
Panel (b): only the plane labels are legible; the exact number of stacked planar slices (three or four) cannot be determined unambiguously.
Chart legend: many composition entries are set in very small type and several heat-treatment variants of the same alloy (e.g. 600 °C / 650 °C / 700 °C + 8 h) are only partially legible.
Chart: no numeric values are printed on the data points or on the three reference stars, so their positions can only be read against gridlines.
